A_MSeiDG2XQ.title: Attributes of the Prophet: His Humour
A_MSeiDG2XQ.one_line: The Prophet's often-overlooked sense of humour: its limits, the jokes and pranks he enjoyed, and why it matters given the grief he carried.
A_MSeiDG2XQ.summary: He picks an overlooked trait: the Prophet's sense of humour, rarely mentioned because Arabs did not prize it, yet remarkable in a man who received revelation and saw the Fire. He first sets the limits. Humour must never mock or belittle, one must not invent stories about real people to get a laugh, though clearly fictional tales are fine, and constant laughter deadens the heart. Then he gathers the evidence: no one smiled more than the Prophet, and the companions threw melon rinds at each other yet turned fully serious when duty called. He recounts the Prophet teasing a man with an eye infection over a date, telling an old woman that old people do not enter Paradise, promising a man 'the son of a she-camel', and laughing as Aisha and Sawdah smeared food on each other's faces. He enjoyed Nu'ayman's pranks, laughed at al-Miqdad's anxious confession over a stolen cup of milk, at Aisha's winged horse doll, and while describing the last man out of the Fire asking about his unlisted sins. He frames this against eighteen close deaths in the Prophet's life and urges listeners to take themselves lightly, joke truthfully and smile through difficulty.

outline.heading: An overlooked side of his character
outline.gist: Humour is rarely discussed because it was not among the traits Arabs valued, so it is missing from the usual categories.

outline.heading: Lightness in a man who saw the unseen
outline.gist: For someone receiving revelation and shown the Fire, his ability to take himself lightly is significant. Speech should always be the best thing to say.

outline.heading: Limit: no mocking and no lies for a laugh
outline.gist: Joking must not belittle anyone. The warning is against claiming someone really did something to make people laugh; a story clearly told as fiction is fine.

outline.heading: Limit: do not make everything a joke
outline.gist: He took life seriously and warned that much laughter kills the heart, leaving it unable to feel or respond rightly.

outline.heading: No one smiled more than he did
outline.gist: Companions reported never seeing anyone smile more, and one said the Prophet never saw him without smiling.

outline.heading: Did the companions laugh? Melon rinds and mountains of faith
outline.gist: A notably serious companion was asked whether the sahabah laughed; they did, even pelting each other with melon rinds, yet became totally focused when called to duty, with faith in their hearts like mountains.

outline.heading: Humour in earlier stories
outline.gist: Telling a frightened visitor he was the son of a woman who ate dried meat, and laughing when thrown from a donkey, both showed his light touch.

outline.heading: Ali's pile of date pits
outline.gist: Ali slid his date pits into the Prophet's pile, then teased him for eating so many; the Prophet replied that Ali had eaten his with the pits.

outline.heading: Dates and an infected eye
outline.gist: He teased a companion with a sore eye for eating dates, who quipped back that he was chewing on the other side.

outline.heading: Old women do not enter Paradise
outline.gist: He told an elderly woman that old people do not enter Paradise, then explained she would enter young and beautiful.

outline.heading: The son of a she-camel
outline.gist: He promised a man a mount that was the son of a she-camel, playing on the fact that every camel is one.

outline.heading: Aisha and Sawdah smear food on each other
outline.gist: Sawdah, the elderly wife he married after Khadijah, refused a dish Aisha brought, so Aisha smeared it on her face, the Prophet urged Sawdah to return it, and all laughed.

outline.heading: Seeing humour amid hardship
outline.gist: In a life full of death, poverty and daily struggle, he found time to joke and noticed what was funny around him, a valuable skill if one knows when and how.

outline.heading: I joke, but I only say what is true
outline.gist: When the companions noted he joked with them, he said he never says anything but the truth.

outline.heading: Nu'ayman's gift of honey
outline.gist: Nu'ayman sent the Prophet a seller's honey as a gift and let the seller collect payment from him; the Prophet laughed and paid.

outline.heading: Nu'ayman and the Bedouin's camel
outline.gist: Talked into slaughtering a Bedouin's camel, Nu'ayman hid; the Prophet found him, heard both sides, laughed and paid for it.

outline.heading: Nu'ayman sold as a slave
outline.gist: On a journey a companion sold Nu'ayman as a slave who would claim to be free; the Prophet's party returned the money and brought him back, and he laughed whenever it was retold.

outline.heading: Al-Miqdad drinks the Prophet's milk
outline.gist: Starving guests shared milk from three goats and saved the Prophet's cup; one night Shaytan argued him into drinking it and he was struck with regret.

outline.heading: A dua for whoever feeds him
outline.gist: The Prophet found the cup empty and prayed for whoever would feed him; al-Miqdad went to slaughter a goat for that reward and found all three full of milk.

outline.heading: The Prophet falls back laughing
outline.gist: Al-Miqdad served him until he was full and then laughed so hard he fell back; the Prophet laughed too at this latest escapade.

outline.heading: Aisha's winged horse
outline.gist: Finding a winged horse among Aisha's dolls, he asked about it; she said Sulayman had winged horses, and he laughed until his molars showed.

outline.heading: The last man out of the Fire asks about his sins
outline.gist: He told of a man whose sins were turned into good deeds, who then asked about bigger sins not on the list, and laughed as he told it.

outline.heading: Humour against a life of loss
outline.gist: He lost his parents, grandfather, uncle, wife, all his children but one, and over eighteen close relatives, yet kept smiling. Learn to take yourself and the world lightly.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: The companions laughed and played pranks while their faith stayed firm.

hadith.gist: Woe to the one who speaks and lies to make people laugh.
Do not laugh much, for much laughter kills the heart.
I never saw anyone smile more than the Messenger of Allah.
Jarir: since I accepted Islam the Prophet never saw me except that he smiled.
The companions would throw melon rinds at one another, but when matters became serious they were men of action.
He told an old woman that old women do not enter Paradise, meaning she would enter it young.
We will carry you on the son of a she-camel.
You joke with us; he said, I only say what is true.
Al-Miqdad drank the Prophet's milk, who then prayed: O Allah, feed whoever feeds me and give drink to whoever gives me drink.
Aisha's doll of a winged horse; she said Sulayman had horses with wings and he laughed until his molars showed.
The last man out of the Fire has his minor sins replaced with good deeds and then asks about the major sins he did not see listed; the Prophet laughed.

maxims: He took himself very lightly

takeaways: Learn to take yourself lightly and smile through difficulty.
Never joke by mocking people or inventing stories about them.
Keep humour in proportion so the heart stays alive.
Use humour to put others at ease and lift their mood.

7:164.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَتۡ أُمَّةࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ لِمَ تَعِظُونَ قَوۡمًا ٱللَّهُ مُهۡلِكُهُمۡ أَوۡ مُعَذِّبُهُمۡ عَذَابࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ اۖ قَالُواْ مَعۡذِرَةً إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَّقُونَ
7:164.en: And when a community among them said: Why preach ye to a folk whom Allah is about to destroy or punish with an awful doom, they said: In order to be free from guilt before your Lord, and that haply they may ward off (evil)

7:165.ar: فَلَمَّا نَسُواْ مَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِهِۦٓ أَنجَيۡنَا ٱلَّذِينَ يَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلسُّوٓءِ وَأَخَذۡنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ بِعَذَابِۭ بَـِٔيسِۭ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡسُقُونَ
7:165.en: And when they forgot that whereof they had been reminded, We rescued those who forbade wrong, and visited those who did wrong with dreadful punishment because they were evil-livers

7:169.ar: فَخَلَفَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ خَلۡفࣱ وَرِثُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ يَأۡخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡأَدۡنَىٰ وَيَقُولُونَ سَيُغۡفَرُ لَنَا وَإِن يَأۡتِهِمۡ عَرَضࣱ مِّثۡلُهُۥ يَأۡخُذُوهُۚ أَلَمۡ يُؤۡخَذۡ عَلَيۡهِم مِّيثَٰقُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ أَن لَّا يَقُولُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡحَقَّ وَدَرَسُواْ مَا فِيهِۗ وَٱلدَّارُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ خَيۡرࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
7:169.en: And a generation hath succeeded them who inherited the scriptures. They grasp the goods of this low life (as the price of evil-doing) and say: It will be forgiven us. And if there came to them (again) the offer of the like, they would accept it (and would sin again). Hath not the covenant of the Scripture been taken on their behalf that they should not speak aught concerning Allah save the truth? And they have studied that which is therein. And the abode of the Hereafter is better, for those who ward off (evil). Have ye then no sense

7:179.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ذَرَأۡنَا لِجَهَنَّمَ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِۖ لَهُمۡ قُلُوبࣱ لَّا يَفۡقَهُونَ بِهَا وَلَهُمۡ أَعۡيُنࣱ لَّا يُبۡصِرُونَ بِهَا وَلَهُمۡ ءَاذَانࣱ لَّا يَسۡمَعُونَ بِهَآۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ كَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ بَلۡ هُمۡ أَضَلُّۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡغَٰفِلُونَ
7:179.en: Already have We urged unto hell many of the jinn and humankind, having hearts wherewith they understand not, and having eyes wherewith they see not, and having ears wherewith they hear not. These are as the cattle - nay, but they are worse! These are the neglectful

7:199.ar: خُذِ ٱلۡعَفۡوَ وَأۡمُرۡ بِٱلۡعُرۡفِ وَأَعۡرِضۡ عَنِ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
7:199.en: Keep to forgiveness (O Muhammad), and enjoin kindness, and turn away from the ignorant

7:204.ar: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ فَٱسۡتَمِعُواْ لَهُۥ وَأَنصِتُواْ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُرۡحَمُونَ
7:204.en: And when the Qur'an is recited, give ear to it and pay heed, that ye may obtain mercy

8:5.ar: كَمَآ أَخۡرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَيۡتِكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَإِنَّ فَرِيقࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ لَكَٰرِهُونَ
8:5.en: Even as thy Lord caused thee (Muhammad) to go forth from thy home with the Truth, and lo! a party of the believers were averse (to it)

8:33.ar: وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمۡ وَأَنتَ فِيهِمۡۚ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمۡ وَهُمۡ يَسۡتَغۡفِرُونَ
8:33.en: But Allah would not punish them while thou wast with them, nor will He punish them while they seek forgiveness

8:46.ar: وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَلَا تَنَٰزَعُواْ فَتَفۡشَلُواْ وَتَذۡهَبَ رِيحُكُمۡۖ وَٱصۡبِرُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
8:46.en: And obey Allah and His messenger, and dispute not one with another lest ye falter and your strength depart from you; but be steadfast! Lo! Allah is with the steadfast

8:41.ar: ۞وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّمَا غَنِمۡتُم مِّن شَيۡءࣲ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُۥ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ إِن كُنتُمۡ ءَامَنتُم بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا يَوۡمَ ٱلۡفُرۡقَانِ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
8:41.en: And know that whatever ye take as spoils of war, lo! a fifth thereof is for Allah, and for the messenger and for the kinsman (who hath need) and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, if ye believe in Allah and that which We revealed unto Our slave on the Day of Discrimination, the day when the two armies met. And Allah is Able to do all things

7:54.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ يُغۡشِي ٱلَّيۡلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ يَطۡلُبُهُۥ حَثِيثࣰ ا وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ وَٱلنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّرَٰتِۭ بِأَمۡرِهِۦٓۗ أَلَا لَهُ ٱلۡخَلۡقُ وَٱلۡأَمۡرُۗ تَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
7:54.en: Lo! your Lord is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days, then mounted He the Throne. He covereth the night with the day, which is in haste to follow it, and hath made the sun and the moon and the stars subservient by His command. His verily is all creation and commandment. Blessed be Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

-03M8xLkEaY.one_line: Reflections on late al-A'raf and al-Anfal: persistent advice, not selling the Book, low expectations, Badr as a stand for right, unity and indifference.
-03M8xLkEaY.summary: He first completes his map of the seven long surahs, which make up a third of the Quran: al-A'raf on indifference as the disease that kills societies, al-Anfal on the laws of victory through Badr, al-Tawbah on the ummah's relationships and boundaries. He then takes selected verses. The Sabbath town shows that you keep advising even the hopeless, both to be excused before Allah and because no one knows who will change, as Umar's conversion proved; only those who forbade evil were saved. A later generation that used the Book for gain warns against any personal interest in religious work. The verse on taking what people offer becomes his rule of low expectations of others and high ones for oneself, while ignoring the ignorant. Badr, he argues, was about reclaiming what was rightfully theirs, not money. The ummah is shielded by the Prophet's living legacy and by seeking forgiveness. Disputes kill a community's momentum, so a diverse masjid needs patience and no cultural baggage. Those with eyes that do not see are the indifferent. He closes by praising the youth at tarawih and defending letting young reciters learn by making mistakes.

outline.heading: Al-A'raf, al-Anfal and al-Tawbah: indifference, victory, boundaries
outline.gist: Al-A'raf shows that indifference destroys communities because salvation comes in groups; al-Anfal lays out the laws of victory through Badr; al-Tawbah sets the ummah's relationships and boundaries, which is why it is stern toward declared enemies.

outline.heading: The seven long surahs as one curriculum
outline.gist: From al-Fatihah's job description to al-Tawbah's boundaries, the first seven long surahs cover the deen in bulk and make up a third of the Quran; the later clusters specialise in single concepts.

outline.heading: Why advise the hopeless: to be excused before Allah
outline.gist: The believers kept advising the Sabbath-breakers so they could say before Allah that they tried their best.

outline.heading: No one knows who will change: Umar's conversion
outline.gist: People are too quick to declare someone a lost cause; Quraysh thought Umar's Islam impossible, yet his name lives on in every generation, so the pessimist advises to be excused and the optimist because anyone may be guided.

outline.heading: Only those who forbade evil were saved
outline.gist: Living for yourself and letting things fall where they may does not exempt you from collective punishment; keep reminding to the last breath with your tongue, pen and network.

outline.heading: A generation that bargained with the Book
outline.gist: Using revelation for money, power or status corrupts the user and endangers the ummah; there should be no secondary gain from the Quran.

outline.heading: Take what people offer: low expectations of others
outline.gist: Accept whatever good people are willing to give; the lower your expectations of others, the happier you are and the longer you keep working for Allah.

outline.heading: The highest standard for yourself, and keep commanding good
outline.gist: The low bar is for others only; hold yourself to the highest standard and keep promoting whatever is known to build society.

outline.heading: Ignore the voices of ignorance
outline.gist: People fail when they expect too much, stop promoting good or give their ear to negative voices; take constructive feedback, but ignorance should not stop you moving forward.

outline.heading: Why they went out to Badr: what only the Quran records
outline.gist: Beyond the events and names in the seerah books, the Quran alone documents why they set out: two years into Medina they were thriving, yet the wealth left in Makkah was rightfully theirs.

outline.heading: Badr was about right, not the caravan
outline.gist: Some saw no need to chase money, but the verse makes it about reclaiming what was unjustly taken; a Muslim never stands down from what is right, which is why Badr is the Day of Criterion.

outline.heading: First safeguard: the Prophet among us through his legacy
outline.gist: The ummah is shielded while the Prophet lives among it through his Sunnah, ethics and the real love of his followers.

outline.heading: Second safeguard: continually seeking forgiveness
outline.gist: Hardships do not come labelled as punishment; whoever keeps acknowledging shortcomings and seeking forgiveness is safe from generalised punishment.

outline.heading: Do not dispute or your wind will die
outline.gist: Taking 'wind' literally: infighting kills a community's momentum and the special quality it once had.

outline.heading: Patience in a masjid of 25 ethnicities
outline.gist: Diversity this rich is a treasure, but it needs everyone to obey Allah and His Messenger, avoid tearing the fabric, show patience and leave cultural baggage at the door.

outline.heading: Eyes that do not see: the indifferent
outline.gist: Those with working minds, eyes and ears who do not reflect are worse than cattle; indifference is the core disease.

outline.heading: Listen deeply when the Quran is recited
outline.gist: Let the words mean something to you so that you find Allah's mercy.

outline.heading: Young worshippers as a sign the ummah is rising
outline.gist: Young men and women standing through tarawih every night give hope to a generation that has had the life beaten out of it.

outline.heading: Each generation must invest in the next
outline.gist: The purpose of a centre is to train, educate and give the next generation space, autonomy and mentorship so they can carry the legacy.

outline.heading: Learning by making mistakes: why novice reciters lead
outline.gist: A polished imam would please people in the short term, but people bore with him from age 15 and the Prophet empowered his companions through their mistakes; anything of value takes time.

themes.note: The Book must serve only Allah and His people; personal gain from it is a sell-out with almost no way back.

themes.label: Character and manners (akhlaq)
themes.note: He lives by low expectations of others and high ones for himself, accepting constructive feedback while ignoring voices of ignorance.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Reclaim what was taken unjustly on principle; giving up on right lets the world order collapse.

themes.label: Love: of Allah, the Prophet, and one another
themes.note: The ummah is safe while the Prophet lives among it through his teachings and real love in followers' hearts.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Continually acknowledging shortcomings and seeking forgiveness is a safeguard from generalized punishment.

themes.label: Unity of the ummah
themes.note: Disputes kill a community's momentum; diversity is precious but requires patience and giving way from everyone.

themes.label: Indifference and apathy as a social disease
themes.note: Societies fail when people stop caring; those who have every faculty yet do not reflect are worse than livestock.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: Young people's commitment gives him hope the ummah is rising; they must be trained, given space and allowed to make mistakes.

Dh4CfbpMfl4.title: Attributes of the Prophet: His Patience
Dh4CfbpMfl4.one_line: Stories of the Prophet's forbearance with rude Bedouins, a testing rabbi, a would-be assassin and the people of Ta'if, defining hilm as staying yourself.
Dh4CfbpMfl4.summary: He builds the Prophet's patience out of a run of narrations. A Bedouin yanks his cloak and demands money, then complains it is not enough; the Prophet keeps giving until the man is pleased and explains with the parable of a camel that strangers chase away but its owner calls back gently. A Bedouin urinates in the masjid and is taught without a harsh word. Zayd ibn Sa'na, testing a sign from his scriptures, demands a loan back early and insults him in public, and the Prophet asks Umar to treat both sides better instead of punishing him. He never struck a servant, woman or child, spared the man who held a sword to his neck while he slept, and answered an accusation of unfair division by recalling that Musa was hurt more and stayed patient. He then defines hilm: not letting other people's bad behaviour make you behave badly, because a person whose ethics change with whoever stands before them has no real essence. The talk ends at Ta'if, the Prophet's worst moment, where he was mocked, stoned and shut out of Makkah yet refused the angel's offer to crush its people, hoping for believers among their descendants, which is why we are Muslims today.

outline.heading: The Bedouin who yanked his cloak
outline.gist: A man pulled the Prophet's garment so hard it marked his neck and rudely demanded money; he later accepted Islam and brought his tribe.

outline.heading: "This is not enough": giving until he was pleased
outline.gist: When the man complained, the Prophet took him aside and kept giving until he was content, then asked him to say so to the upset companions.

outline.heading: The parable of the runaway camel
outline.gist: Strangers chasing a camel only drive it away, while its owner calls it back with a handful of grass; had the companions punished the man, he would have been lost.

outline.heading: The Bedouin who urinated in the masjid
outline.gist: The Prophet stopped the companions from interrupting him, then simply explained that the masjid is not for this and had it cleaned; the man noted he was neither blamed nor scolded.

outline.heading: Zayd ibn Sa'na tests a sign of prophethood
outline.gist: A learned Jewish man who had confirmed every description but one lent the Prophet money for a year, planning to test his forbearance.

outline.heading: Demanding the loan early in public
outline.gist: Days later he insulted the Prophet and his family in front of everyone; when Umar asked to kill him, the Prophet said both of them deserved better treatment from Umar.

outline.heading: The more he is provoked, the more patient
outline.gist: Zayd had read that the final prophet grows more forbearing the more he is provoked, and having seen it he accepted Islam.

outline.heading: The servant girl who forgot her errand
outline.gist: Worried, the Prophet searched for a young girl who had wandered off to play and only said he would have tapped her with his miswak if not for fear of Allah; he never struck anyone outside battle.

outline.heading: The man with the sword: who will protect you?
outline.gist: Resting under a tree after an expedition while the guards slept, the Prophet woke to a man holding his own sword to his neck and asking who would protect him; he answered: Allah.

outline.heading: The sword falls and the man is spared
outline.gist: The man fell, the Prophet took the sword and asked the same question, then let him go though he refused to accept Islam; the man promised not to fight them again.

outline.heading: He could have taken his head at any point
outline.gist: He stresses how easily the Prophet could have punished him, and recalls that he never took any war wealth home.

outline.heading: "Be fair": Musa was hurt more than this
outline.gist: Accused of unjust distribution, the Prophet asked who would be fair if he were not, then calmed himself by remembering that Musa was harmed more and stayed patient.

outline.heading: What patience is
outline.gist: Patience differs from perseverance: it is the ability not to be triggered and not let people's bad behaviour make you behave badly.

outline.heading: Hilm: staying who you are regardless of others
outline.gist: If your ethics change with whoever is in front of you, you have no essence and are only a reflection of them; the Prophet was the same with everyone.

outline.heading: The gamble of Ta'if
outline.gist: Patience was the hallmark of his character; he went to Ta'if knowing that asking for help there risked his return to Makkah.

outline.heading: The worst three replies
outline.gist: Its leaders mocked him with the worst responses he ever heard, then refused even to keep his visit quiet.

outline.heading: Stoned, shut out, and offered revenge
outline.gist: He was stoned until he bled, barred from Makkah until someone granted protection, and the angel of the mountains offered to crush the people of Ta'if; he declined.

outline.heading: Because of his patience, here we are
outline.gist: He hoped their descendants would worship Allah, and that patience is why Islam spread and why we are Muslims today.

outline.heading: His worst moment
outline.gist: Asked about his hardest day, he named Ta'if over Uhud: humiliated with nowhere to go, he was offered a way out and did not take it.

Zayd ibn Sa'na demanded his loan early and insulted the Prophet, who told Umar he should have urged good repayment and gentle asking
The Prophet told a servant girl that if not for fear of retribution he would have struck her with his miswak

takeaways: Do not let other people's rudeness change how you behave.
Correct people gently, without blame or harshness.
When provoked, answer with more patience, not less.
Remind yourself that earlier prophets endured worse and stayed patient.
Hold on to hope for people who wrong you rather than wishing them destroyed.

5:5.ar: ٱلۡيَوۡمَ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتُۖ وَطَعَامُ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ حِلࣱّ لَّكُمۡ وَطَعَامُكُمۡ حِلࣱّ لَّهُمۡۖ وَٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ وَٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتُ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ إِذَآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ مُحۡصِنِينَ غَيۡرَ مُسَٰفِحِينَ وَلَا مُتَّخِذِيٓ أَخۡدَانࣲۗ وَمَن يَكۡفُرۡ بِٱلۡإِيمَٰنِ فَقَدۡ حَبِطَ عَمَلُهُۥ وَهُوَ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
5:5.en: This day are (all) good things made lawful for you. The food of those who have received the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them. And so are the virtuous women of the believers and the virtuous women of those who received the Scripture before you (lawful for you) when ye give them their marriage portions and live with them in honour, not in fornication, nor taking them as secret concubines. Whoso denieth the faith, his work is vain and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter

5:6.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا قُمۡتُمۡ إِلَى ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ فَٱغۡسِلُواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ وَأَيۡدِيَكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡمَرَافِقِ وَٱمۡسَحُواْ بِرُءُوسِكُمۡ وَأَرۡجُلَكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡكَعۡبَيۡنِۚ وَإِن كُنتُمۡ جُنُبࣰ ا فَٱطَّهَّرُواْۚ وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرۡضَىٰٓ أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ أَوۡ جَآءَ أَحَدࣱ مِّنكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡغَآئِطِ أَوۡ لَٰمَسۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَلَمۡ تَجِدُواْ مَآءࣰ فَتَيَمَّمُواْ صَعِيدࣰ ا طَيِّبࣰ ا فَٱمۡسَحُواْ بِوُجُوهِكُمۡ وَأَيۡدِيكُم مِّنۡهُۚ مَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيَجۡعَلَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنۡ حَرَجࣲ وَلَٰكِن يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمۡ وَلِيُتِمَّ نِعۡمَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
5:6.en: O ye who believe! When ye rise up for prayer, wash you faces, and your hands up to the elbows, and lightly rub your heads and (wash) your feet up to the ankles. And if ye are unclean, purify yourselves. And if ye are sick or on a journey, or one of you cometh from the closet, or ye have had contact with women, and ye find not water, then go to clean, high ground and rub your faces and your hands with some of it. Allah would not place a burden on you, but He would purify you and would perfect His grace upon you, that ye may give thanks

5:15.ar: يَٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ قَدۡ جَآءَكُمۡ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمۡ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّمَّا كُنتُمۡ تُخۡفُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَيَعۡفُواْ عَن كَثِيرࣲۚ قَدۡ جَآءَكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ نُورࣱ وَكِتَٰبࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
5:15.en: O People of the Scripture! Now hath Our messenger come unto you, expounding unto you much of that which ye used to hide in the Scripture, and forgiving much. now hath come unto you light from Allah and plain Scripture

5:18.ar: وَقَالَتِ ٱلۡيَهُودُ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ نَحۡنُ أَبۡنَٰٓؤُاْ ٱللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّٰٓؤُهُۥۚ قُلۡ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُم بِذُنُوبِكُمۖ بَلۡ أَنتُم بَشَرࣱ مِّمَّنۡ خَلَقَۚ يَغۡفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَلِلَّهِ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَاۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
5:18.en: The Jews and Christians say: We are sons of Allah and His loved ones. Say: Why then doth He chastise you for your sins? Nay, ye are but mortals of His creating. He forgiveth whom He will, and chastiseth whom He will. Allah's is the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and unto Him is the journeying

5:32.ar: مِنۡ أَجۡلِ ذَٰلِكَ كَتَبۡنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنَّهُۥ مَن قَتَلَ نَفۡسَۢا بِغَيۡرِ نَفۡسٍ أَوۡ فَسَادࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَمَنۡ أَحۡيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَآ أَحۡيَا ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعࣰ اۚ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَتۡهُمۡ رُسُلُنَا بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُم بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَمُسۡرِفُونَ
5:32.en: For that cause We decreed for the Children of Israel that whosoever killeth a human being for other than manslaughter or corruption in the earth, it shall be as if he had killed all mankind, and whoso saveth the life of one, it shall be as if he had saved the life of all mankind. Our messengers came unto them of old with clear proofs (of Allah's Sovereignty), but afterwards lo! many of them became prodigals in the earth

5:38.ar: وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقۡطَعُوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَهُمَا جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَٰلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
5:38.en: As for the thief, both male and female, cut off their hands. It is the reward of their own deeds, an exemplary punishment from Allah. Allah is Mighty, Wise

5:48.ar: وَأَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ مُصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَمُهَيۡمِنًا عَلَيۡهِۖ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَهُم بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعۡ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡ عَمَّا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ لِكُلࣲّ جَعَلۡنَا مِنكُمۡ شِرۡعَةࣰ وَمِنۡهَاجࣰ اۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ فِي مَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمۡۖ فَٱسۡتَبِقُواْ ٱلۡخَيۡرَٰتِۚ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ فِيهِ تَخۡتَلِفُونَ
5:48.en: And unto thee have We revealed the Scripture with the truth, confirming whatever Scripture was before it, and a watcher over it. So judge between them by that which Allah hath revealed, and follow not their desires away from the truth which hath come unto thee. For each We have appointed a divine law and a traced-out way. Had Allah willed He could have made you one community. But that He may try you by that which He hath given you (He hath made you as ye are). So vie one with another in good works. Unto Allah ye will all return, and He will then inform you of that wherein ye differ

5:64.ar: وَقَالَتِ ٱلۡيَهُودُ يَدُ ٱللَّهِ مَغۡلُولَةٌۚ غُلَّتۡ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَلُعِنُواْ بِمَا قَالُواْۘ بَلۡ يَدَاهُ مَبۡسُوطَتَانِ يُنفِقُ كَيۡفَ يَشَآءُۚ وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُم مَّآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ طُغۡيَٰنࣰ ا وَكُفۡرࣰ اۚ وَأَلۡقَيۡنَا بَيۡنَهُمُ ٱلۡعَدَٰوَةَ وَٱلۡبَغۡضَآءَ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۚ كُلَّمَآ أَوۡقَدُواْ نَارࣰ ا لِّلۡحَرۡبِ أَطۡفَأَهَا ٱللَّهُۚ وَيَسۡعَوۡنَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَسَادࣰ اۚ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
5:64.en: The Jews say: Allah's hand is fettered. Their hands are fettered and they are accursed for saying so. Nay, but both His hands are spread out wide in bounty. He bestoweth as He will. That which hath been revealed unto thee from thy Lord is certain to increase the contumacy and disbelief of many of them, and We have cast among them enmity and hatred till the Day of Resurrection. As often as they light a fire for war, Allah extinguisheth it. Their effort is for corruption in the land, and Allah loveth not corrupters

5:78.ar: لُعِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۢ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ عَلَىٰ لِسَانِ دَاوُۥدَ وَعِيسَى ٱبۡنِ مَرۡيَمَۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَواْ وَّكَانُواْ يَعۡتَدُونَ
5:78.en: Those of the Children of Israel who went astray were cursed by the tongue of David, and of Jesus, son of Mary. That was because they rebelled and used to transgress

5:79.ar: كَانُواْ لَا يَتَنَاهَوۡنَ عَن مُّنكَرࣲ فَعَلُوهُۚ لَبِئۡسَ مَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
5:79.en: They restrained not one another from the wickedness they did. Verily evil was that they used to do

5:101.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَسۡـَٔلُواْ عَنۡ أَشۡيَآءَ إِن تُبۡدَ لَكُمۡ تَسُؤۡكُمۡ وَإِن تَسۡـَٔلُواْ عَنۡهَا حِينَ يُنَزَّلُ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ تُبۡدَ لَكُمۡ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنۡهَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمࣱ‏
5:101.en: O ye who believe! Ask not of things which, if they were made unto you, would trouble you; but if ye ask of them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made known unto you. Allah pardoneth this, for Allah is Forgiving, Clement

4:43.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَنتُمۡ سُكَٰرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ تَعۡلَمُواْ مَا تَقُولُونَ وَلَا جُنُبًا إِلَّا عَابِرِي سَبِيلٍ حَتَّىٰ تَغۡتَسِلُواْۚ وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرۡضَىٰٓ أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ أَوۡ جَآءَ أَحَدࣱ مِّنكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡغَآئِطِ أَوۡ لَٰمَسۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَلَمۡ تَجِدُواْ مَآءࣰ فَتَيَمَّمُواْ صَعِيدࣰ ا طَيِّبࣰ ا فَٱمۡسَحُواْ بِوُجُوهِكُمۡ وَأَيۡدِيكُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا
4:43.en: O ye who believe! Draw not near unto prayer when ye are drunken, till ye know that which ye utter, nor when ye are polluted, save when journeying upon the road, till ye have bathed. And if ye be ill, or on a journey, or one of you cometh from the closet, or ye have touched women, and ye find not water, then go to high clean soil and rub your faces and your hands (therewith). Lo! Allah is Benign, Forgiving

Q6f0DasKVGc.one_line: Al-Ma'idah as the surah of covenants: rulings for our purification, fiqh designed to flex, no chosen-people elitism, no flaw ascribed to Allah, and forbidding wrong.
Q6f0DasKVGc.summary: He presents al-Ma'idah as the covenant surah, sixteen sections of rulings that follow an-Nisa's values. The wudu verse is one of the few places where Allah states His purpose: not hardship, but purifying body and spirit together and completing His blessing. The Prophet was sent to the earlier communities as well, easing some rulings and tightening others, and Allah deliberately left matters unaddressed so scholars could reason, which keeps Islamic law alive while other traditions lost their practice. Muslims should therefore stop dividing over fiqh, since they agree on values and differ on details. The claim of being God's children and beloved is recorded so Muslims avoid the same elitism, which destroys self-accountability and breeds blame. The Quran's ability to generate rulings by analogy makes it supreme over earlier books, with rulings serving the five purposes of preserving mind, life, wealth, lineage and religion. A Muslim never ascribes a flaw to Allah, as some did when they called His hand tied, so gratitude in ease and perseverance in hardship are required. Finally, communities fall when they stop forbidding wrong, and Muslims should help Canadian society keep calling wrong what it still sees as wrong.

outline.heading: Al-Ma'idah: covenants in sixteen sections
outline.gist: After an-Nisa's values come the practices, rulings and red lines, arranged in sixteen sections with a closing summary.

outline.heading: Allah does not intend hardship
outline.gist: The wudu verse is one of the rare places Allah states what He wants; when He explains a reason it deserves contemplation, and Islam is not built to make life hard.

outline.heading: Purity of body and spirit together
outline.gist: Wudu purifies outwardly and prayer inwardly; Islam rejects both a pure spirit in a filthy body and a polished exterior over a rotting heart.

outline.heading: The Prophet clarifies and pardons
outline.gist: Revelations abrogate one another; the Shariah eased some earlier rulings and tightened others, so it is neither simply easier nor stricter.

outline.heading: Sent to the people of earlier scripture too
outline.gist: The Prophet was sent to Jews, Christians and all faiths, so no one is exempt from his call and all receive the final version of the rulings.

outline.heading: Islamic law is designed to grow
outline.gist: Fiqh is always a work in progress, not because right and wrong are unknown but because Islam was built to allow new understanding.

outline.heading: Do not ask about what Allah left open
outline.gist: Allah purposely left some issues unaddressed so scholars could weigh evidence, giving Muslims valid options suited to their context.

outline.heading: Why other traditions lost their practice
outline.gist: Faiths lacking tools to adapt as circumstances changed kept adherents in name only; Islam begins with the Prophet and continues through processing evidence.

outline.heading: Do not divide over fiqh
outline.gist: Muslims part ways over jurisprudence though they agree on justice, compassion and tawhid; differences in practice are how the deen was designed.

outline.heading: We are the children of God and His beloved
outline.gist: The claim that Allah prefers a group and will forgive and grant victory without effort is false.

outline.heading: The Quran's critique of earlier peoples is for us
outline.gist: It points out their mistakes so we avoid them, not to score points; likewise a khatib should address the people in front of him, not those not listening.

outline.heading: Muslims and the free-pass mentality
outline.gist: Some Muslims assume minimal effort earns victory and doubt the faith when it does not; Allah's love brings no exemption from consequences.

outline.heading: Elitism destroys accountability
outline.gist: Feeling innately better makes us look down on others and blame anything but ourselves when things go wrong.

outline.heading: The Quran confirms and stands over earlier books
outline.gist: It carries the same values as the Torah and Injil but is supreme because it teaches analogy, letting rulings keep serving their purpose as the world changes.

outline.heading: Rulings preserve the mind
outline.gist: All rulings serve core purposes, beginning with the intellect: one should not address one's Lord while intoxicated.

outline.heading: Preserving life and wealth
outline.gist: The sons of Adam lead to the principle that saving one life is saving humanity; the ruling on theft protects people's property.

outline.heading: Preserving lineage and religion
outline.gist: Marriage rules exclude mistresses, and judging by what Allah revealed preserves religion; rulings exist to purify us and let communities thrive.

outline.heading: Never ascribe a flaw to Allah
outline.gist: What distinguishes the Muslim view of God is His flawlessness; when mistakes appear, a Muslim sees them in himself.

outline.heading: His hands are outstretched
outline.gist: Some called Allah's hand tied during poverty; accusing Him of stinginess after a lifetime of plenty is unacceptable, even in long hardship.

outline.heading: Gratitude in ease, perseverance in hardship
outline.gist: When things go well, give thanks and share; when they do not, persevere and never let the length of a trial lead you to speak ill of Allah.

outline.heading: Cursed for disobedience and transgression
outline.gist: They disobeyed Allah and wronged one another, but the next verse gives a further reason.

outline.heading: Munkar is a social definition
outline.gist: Ma'ruf and munkar are what a society agrees is good or bad; Muslims support what aligns with the Shariah and raise awareness where society has not yet agreed.

outline.heading: A society is protected while it still calls wrong wrong
outline.gist: Many individuals may do wrong, but once the collective stops naming it as wrong and normalises it, the protection is lost.

outline.heading: Muslims as a society's safety valve
outline.gist: Muslims should reinforce the wrongs a society already recognises; marijuana became legal once people stopped seeing it as wrong.

outline.heading: Join the discouragement before norms shift
outline.gist: If Muslims stay silent on what Canadian society still sees as wrong, such as alcohol, it will be normalised, creating a value conflict that is far harder to reverse.

outline.heading: Outro

50c5PFRGOts.title: Attributes of the Prophet: His Asceticism
50c5PFRGOts.one_line: Zuhd as a heart unattached to the world: how the Prophet lived simply by choice and used wealth only as a tool for others.
50c5PFRGOts.summary: He corrects a common misreading of zuhd: it does not demand a hard or joyless life, only that possessions and achievements never own the heart. A key proof of the Prophet's sincerity is that in 23 years he never cashed in on his status or power. He cites the hadith that real wealth and poverty are of the heart, that a poor man in the masjid outweighs a world of the noble, and that the Prophet saw himself as a traveller resting under a tree. The companions echoed his phrase of taking only a traveller's provision. He narrates Umar finding him on a rough mat beside nearly empty jars, the Prophet's warning that abundance would ruin the ummah, the sheep given away except its shoulder, and Mus'ab ibn Umayr buried in a shroud too short to cover him. He stresses that the Prophet enjoyed good things when they came but never sought them or rejected them, often fasting when the house was empty. He was not poor; he chose to give everything away, even pawning his shield to lend to others. The sheikh asks listeners to treat the world as a tool to improve others' lives and confronts Muslims' wastefulness today.

outline.heading: What zuhd really means
outline.gist: Zuhd is often thought unreachable, but it simply means the heart is not attached to possessions or achievements. It does not require discomfort; things must not possess you.

outline.heading: He never cashed in
outline.gist: For 23 years he never took advantage of his status, wealth or power. Those who work for the world eventually take what they were after.

outline.heading: Wealth and poverty are of the heart
outline.gist: He asked a companion whether a lot of money is wealth, then compared a noble man with a poor man of the masjid, saying the poor man is better than the earth filled with the other.

outline.heading: A traveller resting under a tree
outline.gist: The Prophet likened himself in this world to a rider who rests under a tree and moves on. The companions kept repeating his phrase about taking only a traveller's provision.

outline.heading: The wives' complaint and his withdrawal
outline.gist: His wives were upset at how little wealth came home, and he withdrew to an upper room for a month. Umar, fearing a divorce, kept asking permission to enter until he was let in and made the Prophet smile.

outline.heading: Umar sees the mat and the empty jars
outline.gist: The rough mat had marked his body and his winter store was three almost empty jars, so Umar asked him to pray for the wealth given to Persia and Rome.

outline.heading: Their good things were hastened in this world
outline.gist: He asked Umar whether he was in doubt, explaining that others receive their share in this life, and warned that abundance would one day distract and ruin the ummah.

outline.heading: All of it remains except the shoulder
outline.gist: When a slaughtered sheep had been given away except its shoulder, he said all of it remained for them except the part they would eat. What is given is kept with Allah.

outline.heading: Mus'ab ibn Umayr's short shroud
outline.gist: Born into great wealth, Mus'ab gave it all up and died at Uhud owning nothing, his shroud too short to cover both head and feet. The companions never forgot that day.

outline.heading: Zuhd is not refusing good things
outline.gist: He dressed well, wore perfume, liked sweets, cold water and certain foods. He never sought what was not there and never rejected what was offered.

outline.heading: Fasting when there was nothing at home
outline.gist: Many mornings he asked what food there was, and when told nothing, he simply fasted that day.

outline.heading: The fine garment and the handkerchiefs of Sa'd
outline.gist: Companions admired an imported garment gifted to him and he gave it away, telling them Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's handkerchiefs in Paradise are finer.

outline.heading: A servant prophet, not a king prophet
outline.gist: Offered to be a king prophet like Yusuf or Sulayman or a servant prophet, he chose to eat one day and be hungry the next until meeting Allah.

outline.heading: Hungry at noon: the visit to Abu al-Haytham
outline.gist: He, Abu Bakr and Umar left their homes hungry at noon and went to an Ansari's house, ate a simple meal, and he recited that they would be asked about this bliss. People today, hungry only by fasting, struggle to feel this.

outline.heading: Weeping in gratitude for a simple meal
outline.gist: After the meal they all wept. They were grateful for the smallest provision and did not see themselves as deprived.

outline.heading: No three days of full meals, no fire for months
outline.gist: His family never ate their fill three days in a row, and months passed without a cooking fire in his house.

outline.heading: The shield pawned to lend to others
outline.gist: He died with his shield pawned to a Jewish neighbour for a loan he took for someone else, often wealthier than him. Ali had to collect money to redeem it.

outline.heading: He was not poor; he chose to give
outline.gist: There is a difference between someone who cannot make ends meet and someone who gives away everything that enters his house. He had worked since childhood and chose to live this way.

outline.heading: The choice offered to his wives
outline.gist: Allah instructed him to offer his wives an honourable release with wealth or a life on his terms, because he was not going to change.

outline.heading: The world as a tool, and our wastefulness
outline.gist: He lived this way so we could see the world can be a tool for improving others' lives. Muslim societies today are among the most wasteful, while he held himself to a standard for our sake.

bCIPnz0bBLg.title: Tafseer of Surat Fussilat, Part 1 (41:1-8)
bCIPnz0bBLg.one_line: Fussilat's theme that dawah through character beats words, the Quraysh's offers to the Prophet, and why the mushrikin are described by behaviour.
bCIPnz0bBLg.summary: He introduces Fussilat as part of a cluster on how to do dawah. Its name is one of only two surah names that are verbs, signalling that the message has been explained in full detail, yet the surah teaches that character persuades people more than explanation. One Muslim behaving well in the right place does more than a lifetime of lectures, so the best dawah is excelling in whatever position Allah placed you. He tells the story of the Quraysh envoy who offered the Prophet kingship, wealth, status, women or a cure; the Prophet listened to the end and answered only by reciting these verses. From his refusal he draws that ends never justify means and that compromising what you carry cheapens it. In the verses he explains kitab as a collection of values, the difference between hearing and listening, and the image of people on a loud train who can only hear you when it stops, as in Ramadan. The challenge 'you do your thing' means Muslims are judged by their conduct. The Prophet was a human told only that God is one and to stand straight, meaning incorruptibility. The mushrikin are described by withholding zakah and ignoring accountability, which warns Muslims who do the same.

outline.heading: Opening
A cluster of surahs on the route of dawah
outline.gist: Each cluster has its niche; this group advises what to do and avoid when calling to Allah, following one that warned against materialism.

outline.heading: A surah named with a verb
outline.gist: Only two surah names are verbs, giving a sense of action; Fussilat means it has been fully detailed, a whole sentence in Arabic.

outline.heading: Dawah through character works better
outline.gist: Though the Quran explains perfectly, one Muslim acting rightly in the right moment outweighs a million lectures; talk is overrated.

outline.heading: Be the best Muslim where Allah placed you
outline.gist: Not preaching outside libraries or posting online, but excelling and practising genuinely in your own field, whatever it is.

outline.heading: Most early Muslims accepted Islam from behaviour
outline.gist: By the time they attended his teaching they had already been won over by the selflessness and sincerity they observed.

outline.heading: Why Makkan narrations are sparse
outline.gist: Under persecution the companions did not systematically memorise reports, so few Makkan narrations are detailed and authentic; this one is known.

outline.heading: The negotiation period: everyone has a price
outline.gist: Philosophically bankrupt and failing with violence, Quraysh decided to find what the Prophet wanted and sent a wise, respected elder.

outline.heading: The offers: kingship, wealth, status
outline.gist: The envoy offered to make him king, the richest of them, and the noblest like his grandfather, absurd offers to someone receiving revelation.

outline.heading: He listened to the end, then recited
outline.gist: Even through offers of beautiful wives and a cure for madness he did not interrupt; his only reply was to recite the opening of Fussilat.

outline.heading: The ends never justify the means
outline.gist: Accepting kingship to impose Islam was never an option; many offers could have changed his story, including leaving Makkah, but he refused them all.

outline.heading: Holding the winning card
outline.gist: Weak in money and followers, he still would not trade even a year of worship or seating apart from the poor, because he carried the truth.

outline.heading: Compromise cheapens what you carry
outline.gist: The route to truth matters as much as the goal; others have nothing you want, so compromising a word of it cheapens the most valuable thing.

outline.heading: Ha Mim: a challenge in their own letters
outline.gist: The separated letters challenge poets who hung their verses on the Ka'bah to produce anything like it.

outline.heading: From the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful
outline.gist: Allah insists on pairing these two names from the root of mercy despite people exploiting leniency.

outline.heading: A collection of values, fully detailed, for people who know
outline.gist: Kitab means a collection of ideas and values; its worth does not change, only whether the listener perceives it.

outline.heading: They hear but do not listen
outline.gist: Most turned away; like parents and teachers facing someone who understands but will not listen, you cannot force listening.

outline.heading: Veiled hearts, deaf ears, a barrier
outline.gist: This describes their state rather than words they actually said; nothing penetrates despite the capacity to understand.

outline.heading: People on a loud train, and Ramadan as the stop
outline.gist: His teacher compared people to passengers on an old train who hear nothing until it stops; catch them at a pause, which Ramadan provides for everyone.

outline.heading: 'You do your thing': judged by conduct
outline.gist: Non-Muslims fairly ask why Muslims are not better if their book is so great; there is no answer but shame, so the gap is in us.

outline.heading: Interlude
I am a human like you, but your God is One
outline.gist: Knowing only that your Lord is One would be enough to live rightly.

outline.heading: Standing straight as incorruptibility
outline.gist: Standing straight towards Him means integrity: a straight shooter who keeps promises, has no back doors and no hypocrisy.

outline.heading: No superpowers: seek forgiveness on the way
outline.gist: The Prophet had no ability beyond ours; he was given tawhid, the straight path and forgiveness for the mistakes everyone makes.

outline.heading: The mushrikin described by their behaviour
outline.gist: They do not give zakah and deny the Hereafter, and belief in the Hereafter matters only as accountability shaping choices.

outline.heading: What of a Muslim who does the same?
outline.gist: A Muslim who neglects zakah and ignores accountability fits the same description; Allah is teaching through behaviour, not labels.

outline.heading: A reward that never ends for those who do good
outline.gist: Believers who do righteous deeds get an unending reward without being made to feel inferior; it is all about deeds.

outline.heading: Your claim in prayer will be tested
outline.gist: When you say 'You alone we worship', Allah says this is between Him and His servant: live and show whether the claim is true.

outline.heading: Talk is cheap: the reciter thrown first
outline.gist: Among the first cast into Hell are those who recited for reasons other than Allah.

outline.heading: Outro

4:56.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا سَوۡفَ نُصۡلِيهِمۡ نَارࣰ ا كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتۡ جُلُودُهُم بَدَّلۡنَٰهُمۡ جُلُودًا غَيۡرَهَا لِيَذُوقُواْ ٱلۡعَذَابَۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:56.en: Lo! Those who disbelieve Our revelations, We shall expose them to the Fire. As often as their skins are consumed We shall exchange them for fresh skins that they may taste the torment. Lo! Allah is ever Mighty, Wise

4:64.ar: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا لِيُطَاعَ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ إِذ ظَّلَمُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ جَآءُوكَ فَٱسۡتَغۡفَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱسۡتَغۡفَرَ لَهُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ لَوَجَدُواْ ٱللَّهَ تَوَّابࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
4:64.en: We sent no messenger save that he should be obeyed by Allah's leave. And if, when they had wronged themselves, they had but come unto thee and asked forgiveness of Allah, and asked forgiveness of the messenger, they would have found Allah Forgiving, Merciful

4:78.ar: أَيۡنَمَا تَكُونُواْ يُدۡرِككُّمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ وَلَوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِي بُرُوجࣲ مُّشَيَّدَةࣲۗ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ حَسَنَةࣱ يَقُولُواْ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةࣱ يَقُولُواْ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنۡ عِندِكَۚ قُلۡ كُلࣱّ مِّنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَالِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ لَا يَكَادُونَ يَفۡقَهُونَ حَدِيثࣰ ا
4:78.en: Wheresoever ye may be, death will overtake you, even though ye were in lofty towers. Yet if a happy thing befalleth them they say: This is from Allah; and if an evil thing befalleth them they say: This is of thy doing (O Muhammad). Say (unto them): All is from Allah. What is amiss with these people that they come not nigh to understand a happening

4:79.ar: مَّآ أَصَابَكَ مِنۡ حَسَنَةࣲ فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِۖ وَمَآ أَصَابَكَ مِن سَيِّئَةࣲ فَمِن نَّفۡسِكَۚ وَأَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ لِلنَّاسِ رَسُولࣰ اۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيدࣰ ا

4:94.en: O ye who believe! When ye go forth (to fight) in the way of Allah, be careful to discriminate, and say not unto one who offereth you peace: "Thou art not a believer," seeking the chance profits of this life (so that ye may despoil him). With Allah are plenteous spoils. Even thus (as he now is) were ye before; but Allah hath since then been gracious unto you. Therefore take care to discriminate. Allah is ever Informed of what ye do

4:135.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَوِ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَۚ إِن يَكُنۡ غَنِيًّا أَوۡ فَقِيرࣰ ا فَٱللَّهُ أَوۡلَىٰ بِهِمَاۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعۡدِلُواْۚ وَإِن تَلۡوُۥٓاْ أَوۡ تُعۡرِضُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا
4:135.en: O ye who believe! Be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for Allah, even though it be against yourselves or (your) parents or (your) kindred, whether (the case be of) a rich man or a poor man, for Allah is nearer unto both (them ye are). So follow not passion lest ye lapse (from truth) and if ye lapse or fall away, then lo! Allah is ever Informed of what ye do

16:70.ar: وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمۡ ثُمَّ يَتَوَفَّىٰكُمۡۚ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرۡذَلِ ٱلۡعُمُرِ لِكَيۡ لَا يَعۡلَمَ بَعۡدَ عِلۡمࣲ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمࣱ قَدِيرࣱ‏
16:70.en: And Allah createth you, then causeth you to die, and among you is he who is brought back to the most abject stage of life, so that he knoweth nothing after (having had) knowledge. Lo! Allah is Knower, Powerful

5:8.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِۖ وَلَا يَجۡرِمَنَّكُمۡ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوۡمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعۡدِلُواْۚ ٱعۡدِلُواْ هُوَ أَقۡرَبُ لِلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
5:8.en: O ye who believe! Be steadfast witnesses for Allah in equity, and let not hatred of any people seduce you that ye deal not justly. Deal justly, that is nearer to your duty. Observe your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is Informed of what ye do

TM4yeCXLO3k.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 5: Quranic Reflections (An-Nisa)
TM4yeCXLO3k.one_line: Selected verses of an-Nisa: real warnings, seeking forgiveness, accepting mortality, not blaming others for misfortune, humility toward sinners, and justice against oneself.
TM4yeCXLO3k.summary: He frames an-Nisa as the surah of values within the long seven: the Arabs' mistreatment of women was a problem of values, which no ruling alone can fix, while al-Ma'idah supplies the rulings. The verse of skins replaced in the fire is real, so Ramadan is the chance to avoid that end, and the companions, though promised Paradise, were kept awake by such verses. The verse on coming to the Prophet to seek forgiveness affirms his status. On death reaching people even in fortified towers, he warns that Muslims often shelve death because their faith explains it, while people without faith are forced to face it; he urges everyone to come to terms with their own mortality. He criticises blaming envy, magic or jinn for every hardship: good is from Allah, and with the bad one should look at oneself. The verse forbidding fighters to deny a man's declared faith teaches that every believer was once like those they judge. Finally, standing for justice even against oneself and one's parents tests whether one believes in justice or only in self-interest.

outline.heading: Opening
The long seven as a complete foundation
outline.gist: Each of the first seven surahs adds a part of the deen; an-Nisa gives the values and principles, al-Ma'idah the covenants and rulings, and later clusters specialise.

outline.heading: Why an-Nisa: a problem of values, not practice
outline.gist: The Arabs' treatment of women came from their view of women; without the right values, people find ways to oppress even through rulings.

outline.heading: Skins replaced so the punishment continues
outline.gist: He finds this the heaviest verse on punishment because it speaks of continuity and extreme measures for those who reject Allah's signs.

outline.heading: The warnings are real; Ramadan is the chance
outline.gist: Allah destined us for Paradise, but crossing His red lines makes this outcome possible; read warnings with reverence and hold yourself to account.

outline.heading: Companions kept awake by such verses
outline.gist: Those told they would be in Paradise still feared these verses, prayed through the night because of them, and Abu Bakr could not finish reciting this one.

outline.heading: Had they come to you and sought forgiveness
outline.gist: Every prophet was sent to be obeyed; those who wronged themselves should have come before the Prophet and asked Allah's forgiveness, and found Him accepting of repentance.

outline.heading: Remembering the verse at the Prophet's grave
outline.gist: When you visit him, admit you have wronged yourself and ask Allah's forgiveness there; the verse reminds us who the Prophet is.

outline.heading: Death will find you even in lofty towers
outline.gist: Death catches up with whoever runs from it; it needs no cause, since full security cannot stop it.

outline.heading: Every organ carries an expiry date
outline.gist: Live long enough and nothing works, the stage Allah calls the worst part of life; so believers must be in constant preparation.

outline.heading: Muslims shelve death because Islam explains it
outline.gist: Having an explanation leaves many Muslims numb and unprepared; he sounds the alarm from his daily experience of telling people their time is short.

outline.heading: People without faith face death more honestly
outline.gist: With no belief to lean on they are forced to wrap their heads around mortality, while religion can become a painkiller that avoids the thought.

outline.heading: Come to terms with your own mortality
outline.gist: The nafs never accepts its lights going out; knowing what comes next is not acceptance, so dwell on the verses until you are at peace with being mortal.

outline.heading: All of it is from Allah
outline.gist: They credited good to Allah and blamed hardship on the Prophet as bad luck; the verse answers that both the liked and disliked come from Allah.

outline.heading: Stop blaming envy, magic and jinn
outline.gist: Muslims too hunt for someone to blame; sometimes things simply happen by decree, so accept it, and with the bad, look at yourself and how Allah may be purifying you.

outline.heading: Do not deny the faith of one who declares it
outline.gist: On campaigns, be careful and calm; do not tell someone who offers peace that he is no believer in order to take the spoils.

outline.heading: Killed after saying the shahada
outline.gist: In battle some struck down opponents who declared faith at the last moment, doubting their sincerity, and the Prophet confronted it.

outline.heading: You were just like them before
outline.gist: The only difference between you and any sinner is that Allah guided you first; your own faith has been a roller coaster, not a steady climb.

outline.heading: Gentleness commanded even in combat
outline.gist: Allah says this in the middle of war, when life is at stake: be patient and tender, since no one knows when He will guide someone.

outline.heading: Outside war, how quickly we judge
outline.gist: If this holds on the battlefield, how much more in daily life; Allah has rescued each of us from bad decisions time after time.

outline.heading: Upholders of justice even against yourselves
outline.gist: Bear witness for Allah even against yourself, parents or relatives, rich or poor; its sister verse in al-Ma'idah differs by a word that reflects values versus practice.

outline.heading: The hit-and-run test
outline.gist: If you alone saw a parent or sibling run a red light, hit someone and drive off, any hesitation to testify means the value is not yet embraced.

outline.heading: Switch the roles: justice or self-interest
outline.gist: Most people squirm at such questions; if you would react differently were your loved one the victim, you believe in self-interest, not justice.

outline.heading: A verse that looks into the human soul
outline.gist: No scripture asks people to testify against everything they hold dear, yet all we care about is protecting ourselves and our families.

outline.heading: If Fatima had stolen
outline.gist: The Prophet refused to seek exceptions for his own family because the value of justice was beyond dispute.

outline.heading: Justice only when it serves you is corruption
outline.gist: Standing for right only when it benefits you is the definition of corruption; being spared the test does not mean you have embraced the value.

outline.heading: Allah is aware of what you do
outline.gist: The scariest verses state no punishment, only that Allah saw; what comes next is unknown.

3:159.ar: فَبِمَا رَحۡمَةࣲ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ كُنتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ ٱلۡقَلۡبِ لَٱنفَضُّواْ مِنۡ حَوۡلِكَۖ فَٱعۡفُ عَنۡهُمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ وَشَاوِرۡهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِۖ فَإِذَا عَزَمۡتَ فَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُتَوَكِّلِينَ
3:159.en: It was by the mercy of Allah that thou wast lenient with them (O Muhammad), for if thou hadst been stern and fierce of heart they would have dispersed from round about thee. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult with them upon the conduct of affairs. And when thou art resolved, then put thy trust in Allah. Lo! Allah loveth those who put their trust (in Him)

59:9.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُو ٱلدَّارَ وَٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ يُحِبُّونَ مَنۡ هَاجَرَ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمۡ حَاجَةࣰ مِّمَّآ أُوتُواْ وَيُؤۡثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ وَلَوۡ كَانَ بِهِمۡ خَصَاصَةࣱۚ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
59:9.en: Those who entered the city and the faith before them love those who flee unto them for refuge, and find in their breasts no need for that which hath been given them, but prefer (the fugitives) above themselves though poverty become their lot. And whoso is saved from his own avarice - such are they who are successful

gPg05An5blI.title: Ramadan Reminders: Building Altruism and Compassion
gPg05An5blI.one_line: Ramadan reminder: renew intentions and cut distractions, let hunger build compassion and altruism like the Prophet's, and value Fajr above taraweeh.
gPg05An5blI.summary: Early in Ramadan he gives three reminders. First, renew your intention every Friday: ask what you want from the month and what failed last year, and remove distractions such as phone feeds, needless texts and emails, since Allah has already removed some by chaining the devils. Second, the main point: fasting is meant to teach compassion and altruism. Like former addicts who make the best counsellors, people who feel hunger and thirst can empathize with those who have no choice. He describes freezing at an intersection while fasting and realizing he should not judge other drivers whose struggles he cannot see. At iftar the best deed is to feed someone else, and Eid begins with zakat al-fitr paid in food. He reads the verse that the Prophet's gentleness came from Allah's mercy and argues that without it Islam would have stayed a small desert cult; compassion is an exquisitely sensitive test of a Muslim's faith. In the second khutbah he tells of the Ansari couple who put their children to sleep hungry to feed the Prophet's guest, and the verse on preferring others despite poverty. Finally he stresses that Fajr outweighs all taraweeh.

outline.heading: Opening
Renew your intention
outline.gist: Instead of a series he gives three reminders, starting with the one he has given every Ramadan for years. Fridays are checkpoints: intentions get old, so ask what you want from the month, whom you are pleasing, and what did not work last year. Renewal is self-awareness and self-accountability, which is why everything in Islam starts with intention.

outline.heading: Remove your distractions
outline.gist: Part of renewing intention is cutting what keeps you from dhikr, Quran, learning and family: phone feeds, social media, needless texts, checking email, entries on the calendar.

outline.heading: Allah already removed some for you
outline.gist: He began the month by chaining the devils, closing the gates of Hell and opening Paradise; you cannot press a button to give Shaytan a break, so do your part with the distractions you can remove.

outline.heading: Ramadan teaches compassion and altruism
outline.gist: Second reminder, the bulk of the khutbah: beyond the obvious lesson of gratitude, Ramadan teaches compassion and altruism, hallmarks of the Prophet's character. The unpleasant hunger and thirst are the point.

outline.heading: The best counsellors are former addicts
outline.gist: Whoever has lived through a hardship is best placed to help someone in the middle of it; the experience builds compassion and empathy.

outline.heading: Not wanting others to feel this way
outline.gist: Tired, hungry and thirsty, you stop wanting anyone to feel this unless they fast for Allah, least of all a child with nothing to eat at home. Reflecting on the fast is what turns the feeling into action.

outline.heading: Stuck at an intersection
outline.gist: Do not fast toward Maghrib; notice the feeling now. Slow and headachy after work, he froze at a left turn exactly as drivers he usually criticizes do, and resolved not to judge people whose condition he cannot see.

outline.heading: Stop thinking about yourself
outline.gist: Ramadan works only if you reflect and stop pitying yourself over a missed coffee or breakfast; notice what you reach for first when the fast ends.

outline.heading: Feed someone at iftar
outline.gist: The best deed at the moment of breaking the fast is to feed a fasting person, someone other than yourself; you have more food than you will ever need.

outline.heading: Eid begins by feeding people
outline.gist: After Ramadan comes zakat al-fitr, which the Prophet gave as wheat, barley and dates, so that after thirty days of hunger the celebration starts by making sure no Muslim is hungry.

outline.heading: By Allah's mercy he was gentle
outline.gist: In the verse from the opening, Allah tells the Prophet that it was through the mercy He placed in his heart that he was easy and tender with people; had he not been, they would have left him (3:159).

outline.heading: Otherwise Islam would be a desert cult
outline.gist: The Prophet saw the truth with total clarity after speaking with Jibril and the Mi'raj; had he approached people with impatience, Islam would be a small cult among wandering tribes, not two billion people of every ethnicity.

outline.heading: Compassion: an exquisitely sensitive test
outline.gist: Mercy and compassion are the most sensitive test for a Muslim, though not specific to Muslims: if you are not compassionate you have learned it wrong, and the closer you are to Allah the more compassionate and altruistic you become.

outline.heading: Interlude
Who will host this man?
outline.gist: After Isha a man came to the Prophet exhausted and hungry; the Prophet had nothing at home and Madinah was stretched to its limit, so he asked for a volunteer. An Ansari took him home, though there was only enough food for his boys.

outline.heading: Feeding the guest in the dark
outline.gist: The couple put the children to sleep, put out the lamp and pretended to eat so the guest could eat; at Fajr the Prophet told them Allah was pleased with what they had done, and recited the verse revealed about them.

outline.heading: Preferring others despite poverty
outline.gist: They prefer others over themselves even in poverty (59:9): not lacking what they want, but lacking food for their children tonight, something hardly anyone present has experienced. Use Ramadan to feel it.

outline.heading: The poorest give the most
outline.gist: Muslims lack empathy because they have too much; in percentages the poor give the most, and a dollar from someone with two takes far more altruism than a hundred from a millionaire. Those saved from their own stinginess succeed.

outline.heading: Fajr above all the taraweeh
outline.gist: Third reminder: any Fajr prayed anywhere outweighs all the taraweeh ever prayed. Taraweeh still earns Allah's love, but make Fajr the first target of the month.

outline.heading: Outro

6:161.en: Say: Lo! As for me, my Lord hath guided me unto a straight path, a right religion, the community of Abraham, the upright, who was no idolater

6:162.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحۡيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ

6:163.en: He hath no partner. This am I commanded, and I am first of those who surrender (unto Him)

7:20.ar: فَوَسۡوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لِيُبۡدِيَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِيَ عَنۡهُمَا مِن سَوۡءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنۡ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيۡنِ أَوۡ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰلِدِينَ
7:20.en: Then Satan whispered to them that he might manifest unto them that which was hidden from them of their shame, and he said: Your Lord forbade you from this tree only lest ye should become angels or become of the immortals

7:50.ar: وَنَادَىٰٓ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ أَنۡ أَفِيضُواْ عَلَيۡنَا مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِ أَوۡ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُۚ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ حَرَّمَهُمَا عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
7:50.en: And the dwellers of the Fire cry out unto the dwellers of the Garden: Pour on us some water or some wherewith Allah hath provided you. They say: Lo! Allah hath forbidden both to disbelievers (in His guidance)

7:75.ar: قَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِمَنۡ ءَامَنَ مِنۡهُمۡ أَتَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّ صَٰلِحࣰ ا مُّرۡسَلࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦۚ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرۡسِلَ بِهِۦ مُؤۡمِنُونَ
7:75.en: The chieftains of his people, who were scornful, said unto those whom they despised, unto such of them as believed: Know ye that Salih is one sent from his Lord? They said: Lo! In that wherewith he hath been sent we are believers

7:76.ar: قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُوٓاْ إِنَّا بِٱلَّذِيٓ ءَامَنتُم بِهِۦ كَٰفِرُونَ
7:76.en: Those who were scornful said: Lo! in that which ye believe we are disbelievers

7:102.ar: وَمَا وَجَدۡنَا لِأَكۡثَرِهِم مِّنۡ عَهۡدࣲۖ وَإِن وَجَدۡنَآ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَفَٰسِقِينَ
7:102.en: We found no (loyalty to any) covenant in most of them. Nay, most of them We found wrong-doers

7:155.ar: وَٱخۡتَارَ مُوسَىٰ قَوۡمَهُۥ سَبۡعِينَ رَجُلࣰ ا لِّمِيقَٰتِنَاۖ فَلَمَّآ أَخَذَتۡهُمُ ٱلرَّجۡفَةُ قَالَ رَبِّ لَوۡ شِئۡتَ أَهۡلَكۡتَهُم مِّن قَبۡلُ وَإِيَّٰيَۖ أَتُهۡلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ مِنَّآۖ إِنۡ هِيَ إِلَّا فِتۡنَتُكَ تُضِلُّ بِهَا مَن تَشَآءُ وَتَهۡدِي مَن تَشَآءُۖ أَنتَ وَلِيُّنَا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَاۖ وَأَنتَ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡغَٰفِرِينَ
7:155.en: And Moses chose of his people seventy men for Our appointed tryst and, when the trembling came on them, he said: My Lord! If Thou hadst willed Thou hadst destroyed them long before, and me with them. Wilt thou destroy us for that which the ignorant among us did? It is but Thy trial (of us). Thou sendest whom Thou wilt astray and guidest whom Thou wilt: Thou art our Protecting Friend, therefore forgive us and have mercy on us, Thou, the Best of all who show forgiveness

7:27.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ لَا يَفۡتِنَنَّكُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ كَمَآ أَخۡرَجَ أَبَوَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ يَنزِعُ عَنۡهُمَا لِبَاسَهُمَا لِيُرِيَهُمَا سَوۡءَٰتِهِمَآۚ إِنَّهُۥ يَرَىٰكُمۡ هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُۥ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَا تَرَوۡنَهُمۡۗ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ أَوۡلِيَآءَ لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
7:27.en: O Children of Adam! Let not Satan seduce you as he caused your (first) parents to go forth from the Garden and tore off from them their robe (of innocence) that he might manifest their shame to them. Lo! he seeth you, he and his tribe, from whence ye see him not. Lo! We have made the devils protecting friends for those who believe not

3:144.ar: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولࣱ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُۚ أَفَإِيْن مَّاتَ أَوۡ قُتِلَ ٱنقَلَبۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَعۡقَٰبِكُمۡۚ وَمَن يَنقَلِبۡ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِ فَلَن يَضُرَّ ٱللَّهَ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ وَسَيَجۡزِي ٱللَّهُ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
3:144.en: Muhammad is but a messenger, messengers (the like of whom) have passed away before him. Will it be that, when he dieth or is slain, ye will turn back on your heels? He who turneth back on his heels doth no hurt to Allah, and Allah will reward the thankful
